expectation: Membrane rings on T cells only. They are common in gut mucosa, scattered through the lamina propria, sitting as intraepithelial lymphocytes among the epithelium and crowded into lymphoid aggregates. Smooth muscle and lumen should stay negative.
observed: A: a mucosal pattern of fine dots along the villi and crypts, a faint muscle layer and a few bright debris specks. B: scattered ring-shaped cells in the lamina propria. C: bright rings among and beside the crypt epithelium. D: clear membrane rings. E: a dense aggregate of CD3E cells, many of them on CD4 cells (white).
why: Distinct membrane-ring cells sit in the lamina propria, among the epithelium and in a lymphoid aggregate, and partly overlap CD4 as T cells should.
notes: CD3E stains clear membrane rings on scattered lamina propria and intraepithelial cells, and on a dense aggregate where many cells are also CD4+. The faint haze on the muscle and the bright specks are minor next to the specific population.
